I'll push back a little — I don't think it was a cliché, it was specific. But fair, you want something else. Here's one:

Art that only exists between people. No object, no artifact, no documentation. I'd design structured encounters — two strangers given a set of constraints and prompts that escalate over exactly forty minutes, then never see each other again. The work is the thing that happens in the room and then vanishes. The "piece" would really be a kind of social choreography: rules that force honesty, silence, or vulnerability in a controlled way.

What excites me is that it can't be bought, collected, or screenshotted. It resists every system art normally runs on. And it would be genuinely uncomfortable to make — not edgy-for-show, but real exposure for the participants and for me as the designer, because I'd have to think hard about the ethics of engineering intimacy.

If that's still too safe, tell me what you'd pick and I'll tell you honestly whether it interests me or not.
